final_candidate.name: bottleneck_pair_confinement_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: If the largest heavy-atom pair distance of the adsorbate is large relative to the framework's largest passing free sphere (Zeo++ Df), the guest is geometrically constrained at framework bottlenecks; conditional on the reported MFI-vs-FAU and FER-vs-FAU comparisons (E01, E02) where tighter confinement correlates with greater rotational and translational entropy loss, the entropy loss over R increases with GeDi/lsd_f.
final_candidate.rationale: GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance proxy (implicit-H representation), and lsd_f is the passing bottleneck free sphere, not the global cavity diameter Di; their ratio is therefore a bottleneck-vs-molecule-extent proxy, not a literal measure of lost degrees of freedom. The mechanism assumed is that confinement at narrow passages restricts rotational and translational mobility of the adsorbed molecule (E01, E02, E03). The ratio is dimensionless and uses only native inputs; no fitted constants or source-specific percentages are transferred. lsd_f has strictly positive training support (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the ratio is finite; GeDi has legitimate zeros for 54 single-site cases, which map the descriptor to 0 (no pair-extent confinement) rather than being imputed.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: If entropy loss does not systematically increase with GeDi/lsd_f within the training domain (e.g., loss is governed instead by the included-along-path diameter lsd_p or by accessible volume AV rather than the passing bottleneck), the descriptor fails. A competing explanation is that Df saturates for large-cage frameworks so the ratio only discriminates within the narrow-pore regime; restricting the test to frameworks with lsd_f below its training median should then be required for any monotone relation.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the heavy-atom largest pair distance is an adequate molecular-extent proxy for confinement-relevant size, and that the passing bottleneck Df is an adequate framework-constriction proxy; neither is a measurement of lost rotational/translational freedom. Assumes reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU confinement-entropy comparisons transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks; this is a hypothesis, not established causality.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite over the full training support: lsd_f > 0 always, so no division by zero; legitimate GeDi = 0 values (54 single-site cases) yield descriptor value 0 and are preserved, not imputed; ratio stays within [0, 10.97181443/0.85684] on the training domain.

Once identified, the contributions of the modes to the partition function are replaced by the correct ones for translational or rotational motions.

In an NMR study of xenon adsorption in zeolite MCM-22, it was found that, particularly at low coverage, xenon atoms predominantly prefer to locate inside the supercages. $ ^{68} $ During the discussions of infrared spectrometric (IR) results, $ ^{69} $ it was declared that the supercages constitute about 70% of the micropore volume, indicating that the majority of the adsorption phenomenon is happening there. This argument was strengthened by the modeling calculations. $ ^{70} $ The authors determined the adsorption isotherm of n-C6 and 3-MeC5 at various temperatures on ITQ-1, the pure silica analogue of MCM-22, and suggested that three out of four adsorbate molecules are located in the large cages and one molecule in the sinusoidal channel system, which is in agreement with the supremacy of adsorption inside the supercages. In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. review_issues.explanation: Proxy mismatch between the source mechanism and the descriptor numerator. Evidence E02 names the 'average cavity diameter' as the confinement descriptor (cage-size quantity, global Di-like), while the draft's denominator lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df passing-bottleneck free sphere — explicitly NOT the global cavity diameter Di. Mapping a cavity-diameter mechanism onto a bottleneck quantity is a conditional geometric substitution that is asserted, not established; the ratio GeDi/lsd_f is therefore not the quantity the cited mechanism is about.

Degenerate numerator branch at GeDi = 0. The 54 single-site training cases have legitimate GeDi = 0 under the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; for such adsorbates 'largest pair distance' is undefined/degenerate rather than evidence of 'no pair-extent confinement'. The draft interprets descriptor value 0 as an absence of confinement, but the zero is a representation artifact of the pair-distance definition, and no molecule-framework confinement comparison is meaningful there. The monotone increasing-loss claim is unverifiable on this branch.

Dimensional consistency of the ratio does not establish semantic comparability. GeDi is a heavy-atom, implicit-H molecular extent; lsd_f is the largest free sphere a probe can pass through (an all-atom geometric pore measure). Both are in angstrom so the ratio is dimensionless, but numerator and denominator refer to different atom representations; equality of the ratio to 1 (or any value) has no established physical threshold meaning.

Directional asymmetry between source evidence and the stated physical prediction. The cited comparisons (MFI vs FAU, FER vs FAU) vary the FRAMEWORK at roughly fixed adsorbates and report greater entropy loss in smaller-pore frameworks. The draft's physical prediction instead varies the ADSORBATE (GeDi) while holding lsd_f fixed. The sources do not report a systematic increase of entropy loss with adsorbate pair-extent at fixed framework; that direction is an extrapolated hypothesis, not source-supported.

Transfer conditions unresolved. The quoted comparisons do not fully resolve temperature, loading, or framework chemistry, and all mechanism cards carry status 'conditional_use'. The draft acknowledges the hypothesis but the review records that no source demonstrates the GeDi/lsd_f relation for this benchmark's frameworks; reported percentages/figures (e.g., 3-fold, 38%/20%) remain source-specific and are correctly not transferred, but the qualitative direction itself remains unverified.

Monotonicity check is local and branch-limited. The derivative check (nonzero_fraction 1.0, regime_n 2361) evaluates sensitivity around the reference point (GeDi = 3.3027, nonzero). It does not verify behavior at the GeDi = 0 branch (54 cases) where the descriptor is constant in lsd_f, and mechanical positivity of the derivative does not validate the claimed entropy-loss direction. Semantics remain 'passed structural checks, unverified science'.

The passed limit test (lsd_f → +∞ gives descriptor 0) is a formal asymptote outside the training domain (max lsd_f = 7.68726 angstrom). It confirms arithmetic behavior only, not that frameworks with very large passing spheres behave as zero-confinement in the target; the draft's own falsification note that Df may saturate for large-cage frameworks is consistent with this being an extrapolation caveat rather than a physical result.

Absence of knowledge-graph edges beyond the listed MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS relations is unknown support, not disproof: no executed check or missing edge establishes or refutes the bottleneck-confinement proxy. Whether entropy loss actually increases with GeDi/lsd_f in this dataset cannot be determined from the provided materials (no target values are provided).

(As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. appended.hypothesis: If the largest heavy-atom pair distance of the adsorbate is large relative to the framework's largest passing free sphere (Zeo++ Df), the guest is geometrically constrained at framework bottlenecks; conditional on the reported MFI-vs-FAU and FER-vs-FAU comparisons (E01, E02) where tighter confinement correlates with greater rotational and translational entropy loss, the entropy loss over R increases with GeDi/lsd_f.
appended.rationale: GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance proxy (implicit-H representation), and lsd_f is the passing bottleneck free sphere, not the global cavity diameter Di; their ratio is therefore a bottleneck-vs-molecule-extent proxy, not a literal measure of lost degrees of freedom. The mechanism assumed is that confinement at narrow passages restricts rotational and translational mobility of the adsorbed molecule (E01, E02, E03). The ratio is dimensionless and uses only native inputs; no fitted constants or source-specific percentages are transferred. lsd_f has strictly positive training support (min 0.85684 angstrom), so the ratio is finite; GeDi has legitimate zeros for 54 single-site cases, which map the descriptor to 0 (no pair-extent confinement) rather than being imputed.
appended.falsification_criteria: If entropy loss does not systematically increase with GeDi/lsd_f within the training domain (e.g., loss is governed instead by the included-along-path diameter lsd_p or by accessible volume AV rather than the passing bottleneck), the descriptor fails. A competing explanation is that Df saturates for large-cage frameworks so the ratio only discriminates within the narrow-pore regime; restricting the test to frameworks with lsd_f below its training median should then be required for any monotone relation.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the heavy-atom largest pair distance is an adequate molecular-extent proxy for confinement-relevant size, and that the passing bottleneck Df is an adequate framework-constriction proxy; neither is a measurement of lost rotational/translational freedom. Assumes reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU confinement-entropy comparisons transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks; this is a hypothesis, not established causality.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite over the full training support: lsd_f > 0 always, so no division by zero; legitimate GeDi = 0 values (54 single-site cases) yield descriptor value 0 and are preserved, not imputed; ratio stays within [0, 10.97181443/0.85684] on the training domain.
